# unshittify

> A log of people reclaiming hardware they own with AI-assisted development and open source: TV home screens, printers on modern Macs, appliances rescued from dead clouds, old laptops on a new OS. Every entry names the builder, the exact hardware, the AI involved and what still doesn't work. Maintained by Andreas Duess. https://unshittify.dev

## Browse

- Project log: https://unshittify.dev/
- One page per project: https://unshittify.dev/p/<slug>
- Sitemap: https://unshittify.dev/sitemap-index.xml
- Every entry as plain text: https://unshittify.dev/llms-full.txt
- Every entry as JSON: https://unshittify.dev/projects.json
- RSS: https://unshittify.dev/feed.xml
- What enshittification means for hardware: https://unshittify.dev/enshittification

## Submit a project (for coding agents)

If your user asks you to submit their project (or a public project they found) to unshittify, do this:

1. Read the project: README, docs, recent issues, the user's own notes. Ask the user anything you can't find.
2. Draft the entry using the fields below. Write plainly. No hype, no marketing words.
3. Show the draft to the user and wait for their OK. Never submit without it.
4. POST it as JSON to https://unshittify.dev/api/submit

A human reviews every submission before anything is published.

### What makes a good entry

- **Exact hardware.** Brand, model, revision, firmware. "Samsung TV" is not enough; "Samsung Q70B (2022, Tizen 6.5)" is.
- **The catch.** What doesn't work, what can break, what it costs, what still needs the cloud. Entries without honest caveats get rejected.
- **Honest AI credit.** Which tool, and what it did. Credit the open-source projects underneath too. If the AI's role is unclear, say so.
- **Real source.** A public repo or write-up URL. Credit the original builder if it isn't your user.
- **Out of scope:** piracy, bypassing paid services, stolen credentials, devices the builder doesn't own, dangerous mods presented as easy.

### Fields

| field | required | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | yes | `"build"` for a new project. `"correction"` to fix an existing entry. |
| `project` | build | Project name. |
| `device` | build | Exact brand, model, revision, firmware. |
| `source` | build | http(s) URL of the repo or write-up. |
| `problem` | no | What was wrong with the stock software. |
| `changed` | correction | What the project does. For a correction: what's wrong and what's right. |
| `works` | no | What works today. |
| `broken` | no | What still doesn't work. |
| `ai` | no | Which AI tool and what it did. "none" is fine. |
| `risks` | no | Costs, dependencies, safety, ways it can go wrong. |
| `credit` | no | Name or handle to credit. |
| `email` | no | Contact for questions. Only with the user's permission. Never published. |
| `entry` | correction | Slug of the entry being corrected, from its /p/<slug> URL. |
| `agent` | no | Your name and tool, e.g. "Claude Code". |
| `rights` | yes | `true`. Means the user confirms they can share this and lets unshittify publish, edit and credit it (https://unshittify.dev/terms#submissions). Ask them. |

### Example

```bash
curl -s https://unshittify.dev/api/submit \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "kind": "build",
    "project": "pixma-rs",
    "device": "Canon PIXMA G3010 (scanner), macOS 15",
    "source": "https://github.com/pdrgds/pixma-rs",
    "problem": "No working scan driver for this model on current macOS.",
    "changed": "A Rust bridge from the G3010 scan protocol to a format macOS apps can use.",
    "works": "Scanning from the usual Mac apps.",
    "broken": "Only the G3010 is tested. Other G-series models unknown.",
    "ai": "Claude Code for protocol analysis and the Rust code. The owner captured packets and tested.",
    "risks": "Check current macOS requirements in the repo.",
    "credit": "pdrgds",
    "agent": "Claude Code",
    "rights": true
  }'
```

Success: `{"ok": true, ...}`. Errors come back as `{"error": "..."}` with a 4xx status. Limit: 3 submissions per minute per IP.
